literature.headline_zh: 马尔堡病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期马尔堡病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 所有患者均出现发烧、头痛和胃肠道 (GI) 症状,其中 3 例出现出血症状。主要实验室检查结果包括白细胞减少症(白细胞 (WBC) 最低点 1.55 × 103/μL)、血小板减少症(血小板最低点 65 × 103/μL)和转氨酶升高(天冬氨酸转氨酶 (AST) 峰值 1,153 U/L)。一名患者出现严重中性粒细胞减少症(中性粒细胞绝对计数 (ANC) 107 个细胞/μL)。 [10.1186/s12245-026-01370-3]
在 Watsa/Durba 队列研究 中,4.5% 和 1.6% 对 MARV 糖蛋白 (GP) 和 VP40 有血清反应,其中仅包括 1 名已知的 MVD 幸存者。MARV 血清反应性与风险因素之间没有发现显着关联:前往乌干达、接受注射或担任金矿工人。在这 14 名 MARV GP 反应性个体中,85.7% 与其他丝状病毒靶点有交叉反应。 [10.1093/infdis/jiag155]
芦丁排名第一,其对接分数为-10.4 kcal/mol,并且与预测口袋的残基形成氢键和范德华接触。 [10.1038/s41598-026-71976-3]
低弹性观测值在接下来的一年中保持该状态的概率为 82.4%,只有 3.1% 的概率直接转变为高弹性状态。中等弹性观测值有 19.1% 的概率转变为高弹性,有 18.2% 的概率下降为低弹性。高复原力观察结果有 63.6% 的概率保持高复原力,但综合概率为 36.4% 的回归概率。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0357814]
该评论指出,实验性过继转移研究为包括埃博拉病毒在内的选定病原体提供了额外的证据,而其他新兴病毒仍然主要得到人类免疫学、表位或临床前数据的支持。它还指出,马尔堡病毒 的 VST 疗法的开发需要定义保护性病毒靶点、与人群相关的 HLA 限制、病毒序列保存以及细胞疗法具有明显优势的临床适应症。 [10.58460/jccma.v1i01.277]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。

Among the Watsa/Durba cohort, 4.5% and 1.6% were seroreactive to MARV glycoprotein (GP) and VP40, including only 1 known MVD survivor. No significant associations were found between MARV seroreactivity and risk factors: travel to Uganda, receiving injections, or employment as a gold miner. [10.1093/infdis/jiag155]
Rutin ranked first, with a docking score of -10.4 kcal/mol and hydrogen-bonded and van der Waals contacts to residues of the predicted pocket. [10.1038/s41598-026-71976-3]

Low-Resilience observations had an 82.4% probability of remaining in that state in the subsequent year and only a 3.1% probability of moving directly to High Resilience. Moderate-Resilience observations had a 19.1% probability of transitioning to High Resilience and an 18.2% probability of declining to Low Resilience. [10.1371/journal.pone.0357814]

The review identifies that experimental adoptive transfer studies provide additional evidence for selected pathogens, including Ebola virus, whereas other emerging viruses remain supported mainly by human immunological, epitope or preclinical data. [10.58460/jccma.v1i01.277]

news.headline_zh: 马尔堡病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期马尔堡病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: UKHSA 宣布扩大其废水 马尔堡病毒 计划,以检测 马尔堡病毒、埃博拉、克里米亚-刚果出血热和拉沙热等危险病原体。这包括监测繁忙地点的医院污水和废物。UKHSA 还警告医院和诊所对埃博拉疑似病例保持警惕,并在机场和车站张贴海报,告知乘客该病毒及其症状。 [news-d6e6dd6daca87727]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Marburg virus news developments.
key_findings_en: The UKHSA has announced the expansion of its wastewater surveillance programme to detect dangerous pathogens such as Marburg virus, Ebola, Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever, and Lassa fever. This includes monitoring hospital sewage and waste from busy locations. [news-d6e6dd6daca87727]

A new outbreak of an Ebola-related virus, specifically the Bundibugyo subtype, has been identified. The article discusses the challenges in diagnosing and treating rare viral diseases, including the lack of specific vaccines or therapeutics for this strain. [news-99db3c0c272ea7a2]

Bacterial coinfection in viral hemorrhagic fevers raises questions about antibiotic treatment, as the actual burden of bacterial coinfection and the effectiveness of commonly used antibiotic strategies remain uncertain. [news-e184082b1a069ad0]

Decoy Therapeutics, Inc. announced a refined corporate strategy to explore its D-MAVs for a pan-filovirus program using the FDA Animal Rule pathway. The company is developing therapeutics against Marburg virus and other filoviruses, with results showing potent in vitro activity against Marburg virus (IC50 = 1.04 μΜ). [news-5d27f310b71d028e]

A lab candidate antiviral showed activity against Marburg virus in cell assays, with an IC50 of 1.04 μM. This was reported by Decoy Therapeutics, Inc. as part of its broader filovirus program. [news-444b8f1ebbea480c]

papers.title: Detection of Marburg Virus Antibodies 25 Years After Outbreak in Watsa, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: To date, 18 Marburg virus disease (MVD) outbreaks have been reported, most recently in Tanzania and Ethiopia. From 1998 to 2000, a large MVD outbreak in Watsa/Durba region, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), resulted in 154 cases and 128 deaths. Given the public health risks posed by MARV, the lack of approved vaccines and therapeutics, and unpredictability of future outbreaks, this study aimed to assess the anti-MARV seroprevalence in Watsa/Durba. METHODS: Samples collected in May 2023 (n = 313) included known MVD survivors (n = 5), close contacts (n = 22), and other residents (n = 286). A multiplexed immunoassay was used to assess seroreactivity to MARV and other pan-filovirus targets. RESULTS: Among the Watsa/Durba cohort, 4.5% and 1.6% were seroreactive to MARV glycoprotein (GP) and VP40, including only 1 known MVD survivor. No significant associations were found between MARV seroreactivity and risk factors: travel to Uganda, receiving injections, or employment as a gold miner. Of those 14 MARV GP-reactive individuals, 85.7% were cross-reactive to other filoviral targets. CONCLUSIONS: This detected seroprevalence among individuals with no known exposure history may indicate continued exposure to MARV or MARV-like antigens 25 years after the conclusion of the outbreak; cross-reactivity to pan-filovirus targets further suggest the potential for undetected cases.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the seroprevalence of Marburg virus (MARV) in the Watsa/Durba region of the Democratic Republic of the Congo 25 years after a major outbreak. The research aimed to address the public health risks associated with MARV, given the absence of approved vaccines and therapeutics. A multiplexed immunoassay was used to test 313 individuals, including known survivors, close contacts, and other residents. Results showed that 4.5% of the cohort were seroreactive to MARV glycoprotein (GP), with only one known survivor. No significant associations were found between MARV seroreactivity and risk factors such as travel to Uganda, receiving injections, or working as a gold miner. Cross-reactivity to other filoviral targets was observed in 85.7% of the MARV GP-reactive individuals. The authors suggest that the seroprevalence may indicate ongoing exposure to MARV or MARV-like antigens, and the cross-reactivity highlights the potential for undetected cases. The study's findings emphasize the need for continued surveillance and research into the long-term presence of MARV in the region, though the evidence is considered moderate due to limitations in follow-up and assay specificity.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 1998年至2000年,刚果民主共和国Watsa/Durba地区发生了一次大规模MVD 暴发,导致154例病例和128人死亡。2023 年 5 月收集的样本 (n = 313) 包括已知的 MVD 幸存者 (n = 5)、密切接触者 (n = 22) 和其他居民 (n = 286)。

papers.title: Marburg virus disease outbreak and response in South Ethiopia Region
papers.abstract: Marburg Virus Disease (MVD) is a highly virulent zoonotic infection associated with high case fatality rates and multi-organ dysfunction. Early recognition, timely supportive care, and appropriate clinical management are important in improving outcomes. We describe the clinical presentation, laboratory features, management strategies, and outcomes of five confirmed MVD survivors. We present a case series of five patients with laboratory-confirmed MVD who recovered following treatment at Jinka General Hospital/MVD Treatment Center between November and December 2025. The cohort included four females and one male (median age: 18 years). All patients presented with fever, headache, and gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms, with three exhibiting hemorrhagic manifestations. Key laboratory findings included leukopenia (White Blood Cell (WBC) nadir 1.55 × 103/μL), thrombocytopenia (platelet nadir 65 × 103/μL), and elevated transaminases (Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST) peak 1,153 U/L). One patient developed severe neutropenia (Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC) 107 cells/μL). All patients received remdesivir (in varying regimens) and supportive care. Viral clearance was confirmed by two consecutive negative Reverse Transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) tests within 48 h, achieved between days 6 and 12. All five patients (100%) achieved complete clinical recovery and were discharged. This case series demonstrates that recovery from confirmed MVD is achievable with early diagnosis, comprehensive supportive care, and antiviral therapy, even in the presence of severe gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Dynamic monitoring of liver enzymes and viral clearance is essential. These findings underscore the potential for favorable outcomes with early diagnosis and antiviral treatment even in resource-limited settings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 马尔堡病毒病 (MVD) 是一种高毒力的人畜共患感染,与高病死率和多器官功能障碍相关。早期识别、及时支持护理和适当的临床管理对于改善结果非常重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们介绍了 2025 年 11 月至 12 月期间在金卡综合医院/MVD 治疗 中心接受 治疗 治疗后康复的 5 名实验室确诊 MVD 患者的病例系列。队列研究 包括 4 名女性和 1 名男性(中位年龄:18 岁)。
elements_zh.methods: 48 小时内连续两次逆转录聚合酶链反应 (RT-PCR) 检测呈阴性,证实病毒清除,在第 6 天和第 12 天之间实现。所有患者均接受瑞德西韦(不同方案)和支持治疗。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有患者均出现发烧、头痛和胃肠道 (GI) 症状,其中 3 例出现出血症状。主要实验室检查结果包括白细胞减少症(白细胞 (WBC) 最低点 1.55 × 103/μL)、血小板减少症(血小板最低点 65 × 103/μL)和转氨酶升高(天冬氨酸转氨酶 (AST) 峰值 1,153 U/L)。一名患者出现严重中性粒细胞减少症(中性粒细胞绝对计数 (ANC) 107 个细胞/μL)。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 动态监测肝酶和病毒清除至关重要。这些发现强调了即使在资源有限的环境中,早期 诊断 和 抗病毒药物 治疗 也有可能取得良好结果。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据不报告设计限制、偏差、混杂因素、样本量、对照、普遍性或证据强度评估。

papers.title: A multi-level computational analysis identifies Ocimum basilicum phytochemicals as potent inhibitors of the Marburg virus VP40 matrix protein
papers.abstract: Marburg virus disease (MVD) is an extremely lethal hemorrhagic fever with no approved antiviral treatment available, which emphasizes the need to develop newer and safer drug candidates. In the current study, we used an in silico approach to identify candidate inhibitors of the Marburg virus matrix protein VP40, which plays a vital role in the viral assembly and budding process using bioactive compounds derived from Ocimum basilicum . A homology model of the Marburg virus VP40 protein was built and assessed by Ramachandran, QMEAN, ProSA, Verify3D and ERRAT analysis, and 156 bioactive compounds derived from Ocimum basilicum were then screened against it by molecular docking. Rutin ranked first, with a docking score of -10.4 kcal/mol and hydrogen-bonded and van der Waals contacts to residues of the predicted pocket. A 500 ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulation indicated a stable VP40-rutin complex, with a backbone RMSD of 1.98 ± 0.19 Å, a mean Cα RMSF of 1.10 ± 0.52 Å, and a compact, well-preserved fold (radius of gyration 19.77 ± 0.15 Å). End-state binding free energies calculated over 51 uniformly sampled trajectory frames were favourable under both solvation models, at -46.08 ± 5.96 kcal/mol (MM/GBSA) and -27.92 ± 7.63 kcal/mol (MM/PBSA), driven primarily by van der Waals and electrostatic contributions. ADMET profiling, however, revealed a substantial pharmacokinetic liability: rutin violates three of Lipinski’s criteria (molecular weight 610.52 g/mol, topological polar surface area 269.43 Å 2 , 10 hydrogen-bond donors and 16 acceptors) and its predicted human intestinal absorption is only 23.45%, so it is best regarded as a lead scaffold requiring structural or formulation optimisation rather than a ready-to-use agent. Validation of the docking protocol against independent molecular dynamics reference poses gave a mixed result. The predicted affinity was reproducible, and the predicted pocket was clearly preferred over decoy boxes placed elsewhere on the protein surface, but pose recovery failed. No top-ranked pose fell within the conventional 2 Å success threshold of the reference pose. Docking was therefore used only as an initial screening filter to rank compounds, and neither the binding geometry nor any mechanism of inhibition is inferred from it. All structural and energetic conclusions reported here rest on the molecular dynamics ensemble and the end-state free-energy analyses. Gas-phase DFT analysis gave a narrow HOMO-LUMO gap (4.13 eV), high softness and a moderate electrophilicity index, which offer supportive electronic evidence of charge-transfer capacity rather than independent confirmation of affinity. Taken together, these findings identify rutin as a natural lead compound against VP40, subject to the pharmacokinetic and docking limitations set out above, and provide a critically validated computational framework for anti-Marburg drug discovery.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify potent inhibitors of the Marburg virus VP40 matrix protein using bioactive compounds from Ocimum basilicum. A homology model of VP40 was built and validated, followed by molecular docking of 156 compounds, with rutin showing the highest docking score. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed a stable rutin-VP40 complex, and binding free energy calculations supported favorable interactions. However, rutin's pharmacokinetic profile, as assessed by ADMET, revealed significant limitations, including violation of Lipinski's rules and low predicted intestinal absorption. These findings suggest rutin as a lead scaffold for anti-Marburg drug development, but further optimization is required. The study highlights the potential of natural compounds in targeting VP40, while acknowledging the limitations of docking-based predictions and the need for experimental validation.

papers.title_zh: 多层次计算分析确定罗勒植物化学物质是 马尔堡病毒 VP40 基质蛋白的有效抑制剂
papers.source_body_en: Marburg virus disease (MVD) is an extremely lethal hemorrhagic fever with no approved antiviral treatment available, which emphasizes the need to develop newer and safer drug candidates. In the current study, we used an in silico approach to identify candidate inhibitors of the Marburg virus matrix protein VP40, which plays a vital role in the viral assembly and budding process using bioactive compounds derived from Ocimum basilicum . A homology model of the Marburg virus VP40 protein was built and assessed by Ramachandran, QMEAN, ProSA, Verify3D and ERRAT analysis, and 156 bioactive compounds derived from Ocimum basilicum were then screened against it by molecular docking. Rutin ranked first, with a docking score of -10.4 kcal/mol and hydrogen-bonded and van der Waals contacts to residues of the predicted pocket. A 500 ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulation indicated a stable VP40-rutin complex, with a backbone RMSD of 1.98 ± 0.19 Å, a mean Cα RMSF of 1.10 ± 0.52 Å, and a compact, well-preserved fold (radius of gyration 19.77 ± 0.15 Å). End-state binding free energies calculated over 51 uniformly sampled trajectory frames were favourable under both solvation models, at -46.08 ± 5.96 kcal/mol (MM/GBSA) and -27.92 ± 7.63 kcal/mol (MM/PBSA), driven primarily by van der Waals and electrostatic contributions. ADMET profiling, however, revealed a substantial pharmacokinetic liability: rutin violates three of Lipinski’s criteria (molecular weight 610.52 g/mol, topological polar surface area 269.43 Å 2 , 10 hydrogen-bond donors and 16 acceptors) and its predicted human intestinal absorption is only 23.45%, so it is best regarded as a lead scaffold requiring structural or formulation optimisation rather than a ready-to-use agent. Validation of the docking protocol against independent molecular dynamics reference poses gave a mixed result. The predicted affinity was reproducible, and the predicted pocket was clearly preferred over decoy boxes placed elsewhere on the protein surface, but pose recovery failed. No top-ranked pose fell within the conventional 2 Å success threshold of the reference pose. Docking was therefore used only as an initial screening filter to rank compounds, and neither the binding geometry nor any mechanism of inhibition is inferred from it. All structural and energetic conclusions reported here rest on the molecular dynamics ensemble and the end-state free-energy analyses. Gas-phase DFT analysis gave a narrow HOMO-LUMO gap (4.13 eV), high softness and a moderate electrophilicity index, which offer supportive electronic evidence of charge-transfer capacity rather than independent confirmation of affinity. Taken together, these findings identify rutin as a natural lead compound against VP40, subject to the pharmacokinetic and docking limitations set out above, and provide a critically validated computational framework for anti-Marburg drug discovery.
papers.abstract_zh: 马尔堡病毒病 (MVD) 是一种极其致命的出血热,目前尚无批准的 抗病毒药物 治疗,这强调需要开发更新、更安全的候选药物。在当前的研究中,我们使用计算机方法来鉴定 马尔堡病毒 基质蛋白 VP40 的候选抑制剂,VP40 使用源自罗勒的生物活性化合物在病毒组装和出芽过程中发挥着至关重要的作用。通过 Ramachandran、QMEAN、ProSA、Verify3D 和 ERRAT 分析建立和评估 马尔堡病毒 VP40 蛋白的同源性模型,然后通过分子对接筛选源自罗勒的 156 种生物活性化合物。芦丁排名第一,其对接分数为-10.4 kcal/mol,并且与预测口袋的残基形成氢键和范德华接触。500 ns全原子分子动力学模拟表明稳定的VP40-芦丁复合物,主链RMSD为1.98 ± 0.19 Å,平均Cα RMSF为1.10 ± 0.52 Å,并且折叠紧凑且保存完好(回转半径19.77 ± 0.15 Å)。在两种溶剂化模型下,在 51 个均匀采样的轨迹框架上计算出的最终态结合自由能是有利的,分别为 -46.08 ± 5.96 kcal/mol (MM/GBSA) 和 -27.92 ± 7.63 kcal/mol (MM/PBSA),主要由范德华和静电贡献驱动。然而,ADMET 分析揭示了重大的药代动力学缺陷:芦丁违反了 Lipinski 的三项标准(分子量 610.52 g/mol、拓扑极性表面积 269.43 Å 2 、10 个氢键供体和 16 个受体),并且其预测的人体肠道吸收率仅为 23.45%,因此最好将其视为需要结构或配方优化的先导支架,而不是即用型支架代理。针对独立分子动力学参考姿势的对接协议验证给出了混合结果。预测的亲和力是可重复的,并且预测的口袋明显优于放置在蛋白质表面其他地方的诱饵盒,但姿势恢复失败。没有排名最高的姿势落在参考姿势的传统 2 Å 成功阈值内。因此,对接仅用作对化合物进行排序的初始筛选过滤器,并且不能从中推断出结合几何形状或任何抑制机制。这里报告的所有结构和能量结论都依赖于分子动力学系综和终态自由能分析。气相 DFT 分析给出了狭窄的 HOMO-LUMO 能隙 (4.13 eV)、高柔软度和适中的亲电指数,这提供了电荷转移能力的支持性电子证据,而不是亲和力的独立确认。总而言之,这些发现确定芦丁是针对 VP40 的天然先导化合物,受到上述药代动力学和对接限制,并为抗马尔堡药物发现提供了经过严格验证的计算框架。

papers.title: Pathways to health resilience: A cross-country analysis of health system response to re-emerging infectious diseases in Sub-Saharan Africa
papers.abstract: Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) faces recurrent threats from re-emerging infectious diseases, including Ebola virus disease, cholera, measles, Lassa fever, and Marburg virus disease. This study assessed the resilience of health systems in 25 SSA countries from 2000 to 2023 using a multidimensional resilience index and a first-order Markov state-transition framework. Country-year observations were classified as Low Resilience, Moderate Resilience, or High Resilience based on epidemiological performance, health financing, surveillance, response capacity, and recovery indicators. Resilience was heterogeneous and path-dependent. Low-Resilience observations had an 82.4% probability of remaining in that state in the subsequent year and only a 3.1% probability of moving directly to High Resilience. Moderate-Resilience observations had a 19.1% probability of transitioning to High Resilience and an 18.2% probability of declining to Low Resilience. High-Resilience observations had a 63.6% probability of remaining High Resilience, but a combined 36.4% probability of regression. Multinomial logistic regression showed that health expenditure per capita, domestic health-financing share, and GDP per capita were positively associated with High Resilience, whereas internal armed conflict was negatively associated with High Resilience. Southern and Eastern Africa showed stronger resilience profiles than Western and Central Africa, while Central Africa had the greatest concentration of Low-Resilience countries. These findings indicate that resilience is dynamic, unevenly distributed, and strongly shaped by sustained financing, economic capacity, and political stability. Policy priorities include strengthening domestic health financing, targeting Moderate-Resilience countries for accelerated improvement, supporting conflict-affected systems, and harmonising regional surveillance and emergency-response mechanisms.

papers.title_zh: 健康复原力之路:对撒哈拉以南非洲地区卫生系统应对重新出现的传染病的跨国分析
papers.source_body_en: Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) faces recurrent threats from re-emerging infectious diseases, including Ebola virus disease, cholera, measles, Lassa fever, and Marburg virus disease. This study assessed the resilience of health systems in 25 SSA countries from 2000 to 2023 using a multidimensional resilience index and a first-order Markov state-transition framework. Country-year observations were classified as Low Resilience, Moderate Resilience, or High Resilience based on epidemiological performance, health financing, surveillance, response capacity, and recovery indicators. Resilience was heterogeneous and path-dependent. Low-Resilience observations had an 82.4% probability of remaining in that state in the subsequent year and only a 3.1% probability of moving directly to High Resilience. Moderate-Resilience observations had a 19.1% probability of transitioning to High Resilience and an 18.2% probability of declining to Low Resilience. High-Resilience observations had a 63.6% probability of remaining High Resilience, but a combined 36.4% probability of regression. Multinomial logistic regression showed that health expenditure per capita, domestic health-financing share, and GDP per capita were positively associated with High Resilience, whereas internal armed conflict was negatively associated with High Resilience. Southern and Eastern Africa showed stronger resilience profiles than Western and Central Africa, while Central Africa had the greatest concentration of Low-Resilience countries. These findings indicate that resilience is dynamic, unevenly distributed, and strongly shaped by sustained financing, economic capacity, and political stability. Policy priorities include strengthening domestic health financing, targeting Moderate-Resilience countries for accelerated improvement, supporting conflict-affected systems, and harmonising regional surveillance and emergency-response mechanisms.

papers.title: Harnessing Coordinated CD4+ and CD8+ T-Cell Immunity for Virus-Specific Adoptive Immunotherapy in Africa
papers.abstract: Virus-specific T-cell (VST) therapy has developed principally for persistent or reactivating viral infections in immunocompromised patients, with the strongest clinical experience involving cytomegalovirus, Epstein–Barr virus, human adenovirus, BK polyomavirus and human herpesvirus 6. Whether this approach can be extended to emerging and re-emerging viral infections remains less certain. Evidence that virus-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells contribute to natural or vaccine-induced protection provides a biological basis for therapeutic development but does not establish the efficacy of adoptively transferred VSTs. This distinction is particularly important for viruses of relevance to Africa, including Ebola virus, Lassa virus, Marburg virus, dengue virus, chikungunya virus, Rift Valley fever virus and mpox virus. Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) provides clinical proof-of-concept that rapidly developed, partially HLA-matched or banked virus-reactive T-cell products can be administered against a newly emerging pathogen. Experimental adoptive transfer studies provide additional evidence for selected pathogens, including Ebola virus, whereas other emerging viruses remain supported mainly by human immunological, epitope or preclinical data. Translation to African populations will require definition of protective viral targets, population-relevant HLA restrictions, viral sequence conservation, manufacturing feasibility and clinical indications in which cellular therapy offers a clear advantage. This review examines the evidence required to move from antiviral T-cell immunity to therapeutic VST development and proposes a framework for evaluating emerging and re-emerging viral infections as future VST targets in Africa.
papers.journal: Journal of Clinical Care and Medical Advancement

The background highlights that while VST therapy has been developed for persistent or reactivating viral infections in immunocompromised patients, its application to other viruses remains uncertain.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study is a review examining the evidence required to transition from antiviral T-cell immunity to therapeutic VST development, focusing on Marburg virus and related viruses. It proposes a framework for evaluating emerging and re-emerging viral infections as future VST targets in Africa, with an emphasis on viruses relevant to the region.
elements_en.methods: The methods involve a comprehensive review of existing evidence, including experimental adoptive transfer studies, human immunological data, epitope information, and preclinical findings. The review evaluates the biological basis for VST development and outlines criteria for assessing the feasibility of applying this approach to specific viral targets.
elements_en.main_results: The review identifies that experimental adoptive transfer studies provide additional evidence for selected pathogens, including Ebola virus, whereas other emerging viruses remain supported mainly by human immunological, epitope or preclinical data. It also notes that the development of VST therapy for Marburg virus requires defining protective viral targets, population-relevant HLA restrictions, viral sequence conservation, and clinical indications where cellular therapy offers a clear advantage.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the transition from antiviral T-cell immunity to therapeutic VST development for Marburg virus and related pathogens requires a structured framework. The novelty lies in proposing this framework to guide future research and therapeutic development in African populations.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of virus-specific adoptive immunotherapy for Marburg virus and related pathogens in Africa, emphasizing the need for tailored approaches based on local epidemiology, immunological profiles, and clinical needs.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a review of existing evidence and does not present new experimental data. The evidence strength is moderate, as it relies on a combination of experimental, immunological, epitope and preclinical data, with some gaps in the clinical application of VST therapy for Marburg virus.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究解决了评估病毒特异性 T 细胞 (VST) 疗法治疗新出现和重新出现的病毒感染的潜力的需要,特别是在非洲。背景强调,虽然 VST 疗法是针对免疫功能低下患者的持续性或重新激活的病毒感染而开发的,但其对其他病毒的应用仍不确定。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项综述,审查从 马尔堡病毒 T 细胞免疫过渡到治疗性 VST 开发所需的证据,重点关注 马尔堡病毒 和相关病毒。它提出了一个评估新出现和重新出现的病毒感染的框架,作为非洲未来 VST 的目标,重点是与该地区相关的病毒。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及对现有证据的全面审查,包括实验过继转移研究、人类免疫学数据、表位信息和临床前发现。该综述评估了 VST 开发的生物学基础,并概述了评估将该方法应用于特定病毒靶标的可行性的标准。
elements_zh.main_results: 该评论指出,实验性过继转移研究为包括埃博拉病毒在内的选定病原体提供了额外的证据,而其他新兴病毒仍然主要得到人类免疫学、表位或临床前数据的支持。它还指出,马尔堡病毒 的 VST 疗法的开发需要定义保护性病毒靶点、与人群相关的 HLA 限制、病毒序列保存以及细胞疗法具有明显优势的临床适应症。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,从 马尔堡病毒 T 细胞免疫到 马尔堡病毒 及相关病原体的治疗性 VST 开发的转变需要一个结构化框架。新颖之处在于提出这个框架来指导非洲人群的未来研究和治疗发展。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为非洲 马尔堡病毒 和相关病原体的病毒特异性过继免疫疗法的开发提供了信息,强调需要根据当地 马尔堡病毒、免疫学特征和临床需求制定定制方法。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于对现有证据的回顾,并不提供新的实验数据。证据强度中等,因为它依赖于实验、免疫学、表位和临床前数据的组合,在 马尔堡病毒 的 VST 治疗的临床应用中存在一些差距。

papers.title_zh: 在非洲利用协调的 CD4+ 和 CD8+ T 细胞免疫进行病毒特异性过继免疫治疗
papers.source_body_en: Virus-specific T-cell (VST) therapy has developed principally for persistent or reactivating viral infections in immunocompromised patients, with the strongest clinical experience involving cytomegalovirus, Epstein–Barr virus, human adenovirus, BK polyomavirus and human herpesvirus 6. Whether this approach can be extended to emerging and re-emerging viral infections remains less certain. Evidence that virus-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells contribute to natural or vaccine-induced protection provides a biological basis for therapeutic development but does not establish the efficacy of adoptively transferred VSTs. This distinction is particularly important for viruses of relevance to Africa, including Ebola virus, Lassa virus, Marburg virus, dengue virus, chikungunya virus, Rift Valley fever virus and mpox virus. Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) provides clinical proof-of-concept that rapidly developed, partially HLA-matched or banked virus-reactive T-cell products can be administered against a newly emerging pathogen. Experimental adoptive transfer studies provide additional evidence for selected pathogens, including Ebola virus, whereas other emerging viruses remain supported mainly by human immunological, epitope or preclinical data. Translation to African populations will require definition of protective viral targets, population-relevant HLA restrictions, viral sequence conservation, manufacturing feasibility and clinical indications in which cellular therapy offers a clear advantage. This review examines the evidence required to move from antiviral T-cell immunity to therapeutic VST development and proposes a framework for evaluating emerging and re-emerging viral infections as future VST targets in Africa.
papers.abstract_zh: 病毒特异性 T 细胞 (VST) 疗法主要针对免疫功能低下患者的持续性或重新激活的病毒感染而开发,在巨细胞病毒、EB 病毒、人类腺病毒、BK 多瘤病毒和人类疱疹病毒 6 方面拥有最丰富的临床经验。这种方法是否可以扩展到新出现和重新出现的病毒感染仍不太确定。病毒特异性 CD4+ 和 CD8+ T 细胞有助于自然或 疫苗 诱导的保护的证据为治疗开发提供了生物学基础,但并未确定过继转移的 VST 的功效。这种区别对于与非洲相关的病毒尤其重要,包括埃博拉病毒、拉沙病毒、马尔堡病毒、登革热病毒、基孔肯雅病毒、裂谷热病毒和mpox病毒。严重急性呼吸系统综合症冠状病毒 2 (SARS-CoV-2) 提供了临床概念证明,即快速开发的、部分 HLA 匹配或储存的病毒反应性 T 细胞产品可以用于对抗新出现的病原体。实验性过继转移研究为包括埃博拉病毒在内的选定病原体提供了额外的证据,而其他新兴病毒仍然主要得到人类免疫学、表位或临床前数据的支持。向非洲人群的转化需要定义保护性病毒靶标、与人群相关的 HLA 限制、病毒序列保存、生产可行性和细胞疗法具有明显优势的临床适应症。本综述审查了从 抗病毒药物 T 细胞免疫转向治疗性 VST 开发所需的证据,并提出了一个评估新出现和重新出现的病毒感染作为非洲未来 VST 目标的框架。

papers.title: NEXTEBOVAX: ONTCIJFERING VAN ORTHOEBOLAVIRUS-IMMUNITEIT Mechanismen van homologe en heterologe bescherming tegen orthoebolavirussen in preklinische modellen
papers.abstract: The family Filoviridae consists of antigenically distinct human pathogenic viruses such as, among others, Ebola virus, Marburg virus and Sudan virus. Filoviruses have evolved sophisticated ways of evading the immune response thereby causing high mortality rates, and outbreaks are recurring over the past decades. Only two vaccines have been granted market authorization by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) for Ebola virus, yet none for the other highly pathogenic filoviruses. The aim of this PhD thesis is to study the protective efficacy of transgenic yellow fever 17D vectored vaccine candidates targeting the glycoprotein of the distinct filoviruses in small animal models, and with sera derived from small animal models. To that end, we will make use of pseudotyped filoviruses, such as recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses carrying the glycoprotein of these filoviruses, which can be used within biosafety level 2 facilities, as well as a wide range of assays to evaluate the immune response elicited by the experimental vaccine candidates to ultimately determine the quality of the protective efficacy of these vaccine candidates.​

papers.source_body_en: The family Filoviridae consists of antigenically distinct human pathogenic viruses such as, among others, Ebola virus, Marburg virus and Sudan virus. Filoviruses have evolved sophisticated ways of evading the immune response thereby causing high mortality rates, and outbreaks are recurring over the past decades. Only two vaccines have been granted market authorization by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) for Ebola virus, yet none for the other highly pathogenic filoviruses. The aim of this PhD thesis is to study the protective efficacy of transgenic yellow fever 17D vectored vaccine candidates targeting the glycoprotein of the distinct filoviruses in small animal models, and with sera derived from small animal models. To that end, we will make use of pseudotyped filoviruses, such as recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses carrying the glycoprotein of these filoviruses, which can be used within biosafety level 2 facilities, as well as a wide range of assays to evaluate the immune response elicited by the experimental vaccine candidates to ultimately determine the quality of the protective efficacy of these vaccine candidates.​

news.content_title: Scientists begin monitoring UK for hidden Ebola and deadly ‘eye-bleeding disease’ amid pandemic fears
news.content: ENGLAND’S sewers will soon be monitored for infectious diseases including deadly Ebola and “eye bleeding” Marburg virus to prevent potential outbreaks. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has announced it is expanding its wastewater surveillance programme to now detect “dangerous” infections such as Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever, Marburg virus, Ebola and Lassa fever. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has announced it is expanding its wastewater surveillance programme Credit: Getty Images – Getty Ebola, Marburg, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever and Lassa fever all feature on the World Health Organization’s list of health threats While none of the four viruses have emerged in the UK, all are considered pandemic threats. They are included in both the UKHSA and World Health Organization’s (WHO) list of pathogens that pose significant health threats. Sign up for the Health newsletter Thank you! The scheme will also examine hospital sewage and waste from busy locations such as transport hubs. UK wastewater has been tested for poliovirus for more than a decade. During its early days, the scheme – known as Prism – tracked the winter vomiting bug norovirus in wastewater, helping to distinguish between different strains circulating in the country. Professor Robin May, chief scientific officer at the UKHSA, said: “We set out to explore whether new technologies could improve how we detect dangerous pathogens in wastewater and strengthen our preparedness for future pandemics. “Though viruses such as Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever and Ebola are, happily, absent from the UK, this new surveillance means we would be better equipped to spot them early, should they ever arrive in this country. “In addition, this powerful surveillance system is already being used to track more common pathogens such as norovirus, giving us a clearer picture of the behaviour of important pathogens that cause pressures for the NHS every winter. “The diversity of biological threats we face is growing and we need to continue to innovate in order to stay ahead of that curve.” Prism will also look for antimicrobial resistance (AMR), which happens when bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites change and adapt and no longer respond to medication. It may be expanded further in the future to include more rural settings, Raju Misra, scientific lead at the UKHSA, added. “We’ve got largely urban settings. I’d like to expand on the transport hubs; peri-urban they call it, or rural settings, just to see where the animal effluence feeds into that acquisition or transmission of new diseases,” he said. “We want to capture as much of the country and the population as possible.” Ebola is a rare but deadly disease which attacks the immune system and can lead to organ failure, but it is not airborne, meaning close contact with an infected person or animal is needed to catch it. UKHSA posters have been displayed in airports and stations across the UK Red Cross workers dress in protective gear before treating patients in the Democratic Republic of Congo Credit: Reuters There have been numerous outbreaks of Ebola in Africa in recent years, with the Democratic Republic of Congo currently experiencing a major epidemic which has killed more than 3,000 people. In June, in an “urgent publish health message”, the UKHSA warned all hospitals, GP surgeries and other NHS clinics to be on alert for suspected cases of the deadly virus. Posters have also been put up at major airports and train stations for passengers returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. Posters outlining Ebola symptoms and informing passengers on what to do if they become sick have gone up at Heathrow, Gatwick and Manchester airports, as well as St Pancras and New Street station in Birmingham . If a person in the UK were to test positive for the virus, they would then be transferred to one of the UK’s High Level Isolation Units – specialist wards designed for the containment and treatment of dangerous infectious diseases . Only a handful of hospitals operate such wards, including the Royal Free in North London, where Pauline Cafferkey, the Scottish nurse who contracted Ebola in 2014, was treated, and the Royal Victoria Infirmary in Newcastle. Nurse Cafferkey, caught Ebola in Sierra Leone before travelling back to the UK. She passed multiple airport temperature checks before being hospitalised with the virus days after her return

analysis.summary_en: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has announced the expansion of its wastewater surveillance programme to monitor for dangerous pathogens such as Marburg virus, Ebola, Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever, and Lassa fever. This initiative, which has been in place for over a decade, includes testing hospital sewage and waste from busy locations like transport hubs. The UKHSA also warned hospitals and clinics in June to be on alert for suspected cases of Ebola, and has placed informational posters at airports and stations to inform passengers about the virus and its symptoms. While none of these viruses have emerged in the UK, they are considered pandemic threats. The programme aims to improve early detection and preparedness for future outbreaks, with the potential to reduce health-system pressures caused by common pathogens such as norovirus. The UKHSA plans to expand the surveillance further to include more rural areas in the future.

elements_en.time: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has announced the expansion of its wastewater surveillance programme, with the scheme being implemented as part of ongoing pandemic preparedness efforts. The programme has been in place for over a decade, initially tracking poliovirus and norovirus, and is now being expanded to include other pathogens such as Ebola, Marburg virus, Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever, and Lassa fever. The UKHSA also warned hospitals and clinics in June to be on alert for suspected cases of Ebola, and posters have been displayed at airports and stations since then.
elements_en.location_and_population: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) is expanding its wastewater surveillance programme to monitor urban and peri-urban areas, including transport hubs, and may expand further to rural settings. The programme is aimed at capturing as much of the country and population as possible, with a focus on detecting pathogens that pose significant health threats, including Marburg virus.
elements_en.event: The UKHSA has announced the expansion of its wastewater surveillance programme to detect dangerous pathogens such as Marburg virus, Ebola, Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever, and Lassa fever. This includes monitoring hospital sewage and waste from busy locations. The UKHSA also warned hospitals and clinics to be on alert for suspected cases of Ebola, and has placed posters at airports and stations to inform passengers about the virus and its symptoms.
elements_en.scale_impact_and_risk: The surveillance programme is designed to detect and monitor the presence of dangerous pathogens, including Marburg virus, which is on the World Health Organization’s list of health threats. While none of the viruses have emerged in the UK, they are considered pandemic threats. The programme aims to improve early detection and preparedness for future outbreaks, with the potential to reduce health-system pressures caused by common pathogens such as norovirus.
elements_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: The UKHSA is actively expanding its wastewater surveillance programme to monitor for Marburg virus and other pathogens. The programme includes testing for these viruses in wastewater and tracking their spread. The UKHSA has also issued warnings to hospitals and clinics and placed informational posters at airports and stations. The surveillance system is already being used to track more common pathogens, and the UKHSA plans to expand it further to include more rural areas.

Visit our Support pages Trending / Diagnostics & Laboratory Medicine / Ebola and Related Viruses: Background and Issues with Rare Diseases SEP 24, 2026 5:00 AM PDT Share Ebola and Related Viruses: Background and Issues with Rare Diseases WRITTEN BY: Savannah Logan Ebola is a rare viral disease originating in Africa that averages a 40% to 50% fatality rate. A new outbreak of a rare Ebola subtype has called attention to the challenges of diagnosing and treating rare viral diseases. Ebola is part of a family of viruses called filoviruses, which includes the Marburg virus and five subtypes of the Ebola virus. The most common subtype of the Ebola virus, the Zaire subtype, has caused many outbreaks since its discovery in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 1976, including a major West African outbreak from 2013 to 2016. Ebola and related viruses are highly transmissible and highly lethal; they are spread through contact with bodily fluids and have an incubation period ranging from 2 to 21 days. People infected with Ebola are contagious when they start showing signs and symptoms, which can initially include headache, fever, anorexia, and malaise. These are often followed by nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Ultimately, Ebola can lead to multi-organ failure, internal and external bleeding, and death. A licensed vaccine has been developed for the Zaire strain of Ebola, and considerable progress has been made in the development of vaccines for the Sudan strain of Ebola and the Marburg virus. However, a recent outbreak of an Ebola-related virus has been identified as the Bundibugyo subtype, which currently has no specific vaccines or therapeutics. The Bundibugyo strain has caused only two previous outbreaks, and the current outbreak has already surpassed both previous outbreaks in scale and trajectory. The rapid growth of the most recent Bundibugyo outbreak can be partially attributed to delays in detection of the virus and confirmed diagnoses via laboratory testing. Access to laboratories is limited in many parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo, and samples sometimes have to travel large distances to reach reference laboratories. This outbreak also highlights the danger of overlooking rare infectious diseases; medical countermeasures could have stopped much of the outbreak if put in place sooner. Better preparation through the creation of vaccines and diagnostics tests, as well as quicker coordination of health systems across borders, may help prevent or slow future rare disease outbreaks. Sources: The New England Journal of Medicine, Science Daily, StatPearls Share About the Author Savannah Logan Doctorate (PhD) Savannah (she/her) is a scientific writer specializing in cardiology at Labroots. Her background is in medical writing with significant experience in obesity, oncology, and infectious diseases. She has conducted research in microbial biophysics, optics, and education. She received her Ph.D. from the University of Oregon. Visit our Support pages Trending / Diagnostics & Laboratory Medicine / Ebola and Related Viruses: Background and Issues with Rare Diseases SEP 24, 2026 5:00 AM PDT Share Ebola and Related Viruses: Background and Issues with Rare Diseases WRITTEN BY: Savannah Logan Ebola is a rare viral disease originating in Africa that averages a 40% to 50% fatality rate. A new outbreak of a rare Ebola subtype has called attention to the challenges of diagnosing and treating rare viral diseases. Ebola is part of a family of viruses called filoviruses, which includes the Marburg virus and five subtypes of the Ebola virus. The most common subtype of the Ebola virus, the Zaire subtype, has caused many outbreaks since its discovery in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 1976, including a major West African outbreak from 2013 to 2016. Ebola and related viruses are highly transmissible and highly lethal; they are spread through contact with bodily fluids and have an incubation period ranging from 2 to 21 days. People infected with Ebola are contagious when they start showing signs and symptoms, which can initially include headache, fever, anorexia, and malaise. These are often followed by nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Ultimately, Ebola can lead to multi-organ failure, internal and external bleeding, and death. A licensed vaccine has been developed for the Zaire strain of Ebola, and considerable progress has been made in the development of vaccines for the Sudan strain of Ebola and the Marburg virus. However, a recent outbreak of an Ebola-related virus has been identified as the Bundibugyo subtype, which currently has no specific vaccines or therapeutics. The Bundibugyo strain has caused only two previous outbreaks, and the current outbreak has already surpassed both previous outbreaks in scale and trajectory. The rapid growth of the most recent Bundibugyo outbreak can be partially attributed to delays in detection of the virus and confirmed diagnoses via laboratory testing. Access to laboratories is limited in many parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo, and samples sometimes have to travel large distances to reach reference laboratories. This outbreak also highlights the danger of overlooking rare infectious diseases; medical countermeasures could have stopped much of the outbreak if put in place sooner. Better preparation through the creation of vaccines and diagnostics tests, as well as quicker coordination of health systems across borders, may help prevent or slow future rare disease outbreaks. Sources: The New England Journal of Medicine, Science Daily, StatPearls Share About the Author Savannah Logan Doctorate (PhD) Savannah (she/her) is a scientific writer specializing in cardiology at Labroots. Her background is in medical writing with significant experience in obesity, oncology, and infectious diseases. She has conducted research in microbial biophysics, optics, and education. She received her Ph.D. from the University of Oregon. news.content: Morningstar Capabilities and Products Company Portfolio Tools Sections Markets Funds ETFs Stocks Bonds Investing Ideas For Advisors Home Tools Portfolio Watchlists Screener Compare Chart Rating Changes Sections Markets Funds ETFs Stocks Bonds Investing Ideas For Advisors Media Help What’s New Notifications Products for Investors All Products and Services Home News PR Newswire /C O R R E C T I O N — Decoy Therapeutics, Inc/ /C O R R E C T I O N — Decoy Therapeutics, Inc/ Provided by PR Newswire Sep 22, 2026, 6:03:00 PM /C O R R E C T I O N -- Decoy Therapeutics, Inc/ /C O R R E C T I O N -- Decoy Therapeutics, Inc/ PR Newswire CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Sept. 22, 2026 In the news release, Decoy Therapeutics Exploring Pan-Filovirus Program via FDA Animal Rule Pathway and Non-Dilutive Funding, issued 22-Sep-2026 by Decoy Therapeutics, Inc over PR Newswire, we are advised by the company that the original version contained incorrect information introduced by PR Newswire during transmission. The complete, corrected release follows, with additional details at the end: Decoy Therapeutics Exploring Pan-Filovirus Program via FDA Animal Rule Pathway and Non-Dilutive Funding Next-Generation D-MAVsTM Demonstrate Potent In Vitro Activity Against Ebola Zaire and Marburg Viruses; Targeting High-Value FDA Priority Review Voucher Eligibility CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Decoy Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: DCOY), a biotechnology company pioneering Designable Multi-Antivirals (D-MAVsTM) to target major respiratory and high consequence viral threats, today announced a refined corporate strategy to explore its D-MAVs for additional candidates, including a pan-filovirus program along the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Animal Rule pathway for expedited regulatory approval. Based on recent encouraging discussions, the Company is actively pursuing non-dilutive government grants and public health partnerships to support the preclinical and clinical development of its broad-spectrum biodefense pipeline with monetization potential upon approval via Priority Review Voucher (PRV) opportunities. Platform Velocity & Preclinical Breakthroughs Following the discovery of initial cross-viral activity from Decoy's pan-coronavirus fusion inhibitors against wild-type Ebola Zaire and Lassa fever virus (announced July 27, 2026), Decoy initiated a dedicated program to de novo design filovirus fusion inhibitors using its AI/ML-driven IMP3ACTTM computational engine. Key highlights include: Ebola Zaire Potency: A first-generation de novo candidate achieved a low-micromolar half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 1.56 μΜ against wild-type Ebola Zaire virus in cell-based assays, a > five-fold improvement in potency vs. the pan-coronavirus lead, and a 7-fold improvement over the benchmark antiviral, remdesivir. Marburg Virus Activity: This candidate also demonstrated potent cross-family activity against Marburg virus (IC50 = 1.04 μΜ). Pan-Filovirus Objective: Decoy is executing generative design campaigns to establish a single, broad-spectrum pan-filovirus D-MAV for pre- and post-exposure prophylaxis against all human-infecting filoviruses. Engineered for Extended Protection & Prophylactic Utility Effective prophylaxis against high-consequence viral pathogens requires sustained drug levels at the site of infection ingress. Beyond optimizing binding potency, Decoy's IMP3ACT platform structurally engineers molecules for extended tissue residence time and long systemic plasma half-lives, with potential for weekly dosing. analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 该报告强调了 Decoy 的泛 丝状病毒 方法应对多种 丝状病毒 的潜力,包括扎伊尔埃博拉病毒、马尔堡病毒、苏丹病毒和本迪布焦病毒。丝状病毒 的历史 死亡率 率范围在 40% 至 90% 之间,当前的本迪布焦病毒 暴发 强调了对广谱治疗的需要。

news.content: Please enable Javascript Subscribe Breast Cancers Today Derm Immuno Today Gastro Today Heme Today Metabolic Care Today Nephrology Times Neuro Therapy Today Pulmonology Today More Infectious DiseaseBacterial Coinfection in Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers Raises Questions About Antibiotic Treatment Infectious Disease Bacterial Coinfection in Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers Raises Questions About Antibiotic Treatment Published: September 23, 2026 By LF Leslie Feldman A systematic review published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases examined the frequency, microbiology, and clinical significance of bacterial coinfection among patients with four high-consequence viral infections (HCVIs): Ebola virus disease (EVD), Marburg virus disease (MVD), Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF), and Lassa fever (LF). Because bacterial sepsis can resemble or complicate these viral illnesses, clinicians frequently administer empiric antibiotics. However, the actual burden of bacterial coinfection and the effectiveness of commonly used antibiotic strategies remain uncertain. Advertisement The authors reviewed 30 publications, including case reports, cohort studies, and cross-sectional studies, that described bacterial coinfection in patients with these diseases. Bacteremia was reported most often in patients with CCHF, with 46 cases, followed by 16 cases each among patients with EVD and MVD and two cases among patients with Lassa fever. Among 27 patients with EVD treated outside Africa, seven (26%) were reported to have bacterial coinfection. Across the HCVIs examined, bloodstream infections were generally identified relatively late in the disease course, with bacteremia occurring a median of 11 days after symptom onset and ranging from the day of symptom onset to 23 days afterward. The organisms responsible for infection were diverse. Reported pathogens included enteric bacteria, healthcare-associated organisms, opportunistic pathogens, and zoonotic bacteria. A particularly important finding involved Brucella species among patients with CCHF, highlighting the need to consider exposure history and regional epidemiology when selecting antimicrobial treatment. The diversity of organisms also raises concerns about relying on a single empiric antibiotic regimen for patients with these infections. Ceftriaxone was the most frequently reported empiric antibiotic. However, the review found that ceftriaxone was predicted to be active against only a minority of bloodstream isolates. This finding is clinically important because empiric antibiotic therapy is intended to provide early protection against potentially fatal bacterial infections. If commonly selected antibiotics do not adequately cover the organisms involved, treatment may provide limited benefit while potentially contributing to antimicrobial resistance and unnecessary antibiotic exposure. The relationship between bacterial coinfection and mortality also varied by viral disease. Among patients with EVD or MVD, mortality appeared similar regardless of whether bacterial coinfection was identified. In contrast, patients with CCHF with bacterial coinfection experienced substantially higher mortality than those without coinfection: 15.5% compared with 5.7%. This association suggests that bacterial infection may be particularly important in CCHF, although the available evidence cannot establish causation. The authors emphasize that current evidence is insufficient to determine the true incidence or clinical impact of bacterial coinfection in HCVIs. Small sample sizes, inconsistent diagnostic approaches, and differences in clinical settings limit many available studies. Consequently, clinicians must often make antibiotic decisions with incomplete information. The study concludes that prospective research using standardized bacterial diagnostic methods and systematic antimicrobial-resistance testing is urgently needed. Better evidence could help clinicians distinguish viral disease from bacterial coinfection, select more appropriate empiric antibiotics, and reduce unnecessary antimicrobial use. The review highlights an important but poorly understood complication of severe viral hemorrhagic diseases and underscores the need for evidence-based antimicrobial strategies. References Page B, et al. Open Forum Infect Dis. 2026;13(8):ofag404. analysis.brief_en: A systematic review published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases examined bacterial coinfection in patients with four high-consequence viral infections: Ebola virus disease (EVD), Marburg virus disease (MVD), Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF), and Lassa fever (LF). The study reviewed 30 publications, including case reports, cohort studies, and cross-sectional studies, highlighting that bacterial coinfection is a significant but poorly understood complication of these severe viral diseases. Bacteremia was most frequently reported in CCHF patients, with 46 cases, followed by 16 cases each in EVD and MVD, and two in Lassa fever. Among EVD and MVD patients treated outside Africa, 26% had bacterial coinfection. However, the review found that commonly used antibiotics like ceftriaxone may not adequately cover the diverse pathogens involved, potentially leading to limited treatment benefits and contributing to antimicrobial resistance. The authors stress that current evidence is insufficient to determine the true incidence or clinical impact of bacterial coinfection in these diseases, and they call for prospective research using standardized diagnostic methods and antimicrobial-resistance testing to improve treatment strategies and reduce unnecessary antibiotic use.

elements_zh.time: 《传染病开放论坛》上发表的一篇系统综述研究了四种高后果病毒感染 (HCVI) 患者细菌合并感染的频率、微生物学和临床意义:埃博拉病毒病 (EVD)、马尔堡病毒病 (MVD)、克里米亚-刚果出血热 (CCHF) 和拉沙热 (LF)。
elements_zh.location_and_population: 该研究回顾了 30 篇出版物,包括 病例报告、队列研究 研究和横断面研究,描述了患有这些疾病的患者的细菌合并感染。
elements_zh.event: 病毒性出血热中的细菌合并感染引发了有关抗生素 治疗 的问题,因为细菌合并感染的实际负担和常用抗生素策略的有效性仍不确定。
elements_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: CCHF 患者最常报告菌血症,有 46 例,其次是 EVD 和 MVD 患者各 16 例,拉沙热患者各 2 例。细菌合并感染与 死亡率 之间的关系因病毒性疾病而异,当存在合并感染时,CCHF 患者的 死亡率 (15.5%) 明显高于不存在合并感染的患者 (5.7%)。
elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 作者强调,目前的证据不足以确定细菌合并感染对 HCVI 的真正 发病率 或临床影响。小样本量、不一致的诊断方法以及临床环境的差异限制了许多可用的研究。迫切需要使用标准化细菌诊断方法和系统的抗菌药物耐药性测试进行前瞻性研究。

analysis_en.time: A systematic review published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases examined the frequency, microbiology, and clinical significance of bacterial coinfection among patients with four high-consequence viral infections (HCVIs): Ebola virus disease (EVD), Marburg virus disease (MVD), Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF), and Lassa fever (LF).
analysis_en.location_and_population: The study reviewed 30 publications, including case reports, cohort studies, and cross-sectional studies, that described bacterial coinfection in patients with these diseases.
analysis_en.event: Bacterial coinfection in viral hemorrhagic fevers raises questions about antibiotic treatment, as the actual burden of bacterial coinfection and the effectiveness of commonly used antibiotic strategies remain uncertain.
analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: Bacteremia was reported most often in patients with CCHF, with 46 cases, followed by 16 cases each among patients with EVD and MVD and two cases among patients with Lassa fever. The relationship between bacterial coinfection and mortality varied by viral disease, with patients with CCHF experiencing substantially higher mortality (15.5%) when coinfection was present compared to those without (5.7%).
analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: The authors emphasize that current evidence is insufficient to determine the true incidence or clinical impact of bacterial coinfection in HCVIs. Small sample sizes, inconsistent diagnostic approaches, and differences in clinical settings limit many available studies. Prospective research using standardized bacterial diagnostic methods and systematic antimicrobial-resistance testing is urgently needed.

news.title_zh: 病毒性出血热中的细菌混合感染引发了关于抗生素 治疗 的疑问 - DocWireNews
news.source_body_en: A systematic review published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases examined bacterial coinfection in patients with four high-consequence viral infections: Ebola virus disease (EVD), Marburg virus disease (MVD), Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF), and Lassa fever (LF). The study reviewed 30 publications, including case reports, cohort studies, and cross-sectional studies, highlighting that bacterial coinfection is a significant but poorly understood complication of these severe viral diseases. Bacteremia was most frequently reported in CCHF patients, with 46 cases, followed by 16 cases each in EVD and MVD, and two in Lassa fever. Among EVD and MVD patients treated outside Africa, 26% had bacterial coinfection. However, the review found that commonly used antibiotics like ceftriaxone may not adequately cover the diverse pathogens involved, potentially leading to limited treatment benefits and contributing to antimicrobial resistance. The authors stress that current evidence is insufficient to determine the true incidence or clinical impact of bacterial coinfection in these diseases, and they call for prospective research using standardized diagnostic methods and antimicrobial-resistance testing to improve treatment strategies and reduce unnecessary antibiotic use.

Key Terms animal rule, half-maximal inhibitory concentration (ic50), priority review voucher, non-dilutive funding, +1 more 5 terms animal rule regulatory "FDA Animal Rule pathway for expedited regulatory approval" A regulatory pathway that allows safety and effectiveness of drugs or vaccines to be judged primarily from well-controlled animal studies when human trials would be unethical or impossible, such as for treatments against rare, lethal exposures. It matters to investors because approval via this route can speed a product to market for urgent or niche needs but carries extra scientific and regulatory risk—think of it as accepting a high-quality dress rehearsal instead of a live show, with requirements for strong animal models and often additional post-approval obligations. half-maximal inhibitory concentration (ic50) medical "low-micromolar half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 1.56" The half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) is the concentration of a drug, antibody, or other molecule required to reduce a specific biological activity (such as enzyme action, cell growth, or receptor signaling) by 50% in a controlled lab assay. It measures potency: lower IC50 means a smaller amount of substance is needed to produce that half‐reduction, like needing less salt to make a soup noticeably less salty. For investors, IC50 helps compare how potent competing drug candidates are and informs early-stage development, dosing expectations, and risk assessments. priority review voucher regulatory "FDA's Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV) Program" A priority review voucher is a transferable regulatory incentive that lets a company move a future drug or device application to the front of the review line, shortening the review period by several months. For investors it matters because the voucher can speed up market access for a high-value product or be sold to other companies for significant cash, acting like a tradable fast-pass that can accelerate revenue or create immediate financial upside. non-dilutive funding financial "actively pursuing non-dilutive government grants" Non-dilutive funding is money a company raises that does not require issuing new shares or reducing existing owners’ percentage ownership, such as grants, certain loans, contract revenue, or licensing deals. It matters to investors because it lets a company finance growth or research without shrinking shareholder stakes or changing control, much like topping up a car’s gas tank instead of selling part of the car to pay for the trip. in vitro technical "demonstrate potent In Vitro Activity Against Ebola Zaire" In vitro describes laboratory tests performed on cells, tissues, or biological molecules outside a living body—literally “in glass,” such as in test tubes or dishes. For investors, in vitro results are an early sign that a drug or technology has a desired effect under controlled conditions, but they don’t guarantee it will work or be safe in animals or people; think of them as a prototype tested on a bench rather than in real-world use. The complete, corrected release follows, with additional details at the end: Decoy Therapeutics Exploring Pan-Filovirus Program via FDA Animal Rule Pathway and Non-Dilutive Funding Next-Generation D-MAVsTM Demonstrate Potent In Vitro Activity Against Ebola Zaire and Marburg Viruses; Targeting High-Value FDA Priority Review Voucher Eligibility CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Decoy Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: DCOY), a biotechnology company pioneering Designable Multi-Antivirals (D-MAVsTM) to target major respiratory and high consequence viral threats, today announced a refined corporate strategy to explore its D-MAVs for additional candidates, including a pan-filovirus program along the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Animal Rule pathway for expedited regulatory approval. Based on recent encouraging discussions, the Company is actively pursuing non-dilutive government grants and public health partnerships to support the preclinical and clinical development of its broad-spectrum biodefense pipeline with monetization potential upon approval via Priority Review Voucher (PRV) opportunities. Platform Velocity & Preclinical Breakthroughs Following the discovery of initial cross-viral activity from Decoy's pan-coronavirus fusion inhibitors against wild-type Ebola Zaire and Lassa fever virus (announced July 27, 2026), Decoy initiated a dedicated program to de novo design filovirus fusion inhibitors using its AI/ML-driven IMP3ACTTM computational engine. Key highlights include: Ebola Zaire Potency: A first-generation de novo candidate achieved a low-micromolar half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 1.56 μΜ against wild-type Ebola Zaire virus in cell-based assays, a > five-fold improvement in potency vs. the pan-coronavirus lead, and a 7-fold improvement over the benchmark antiviral, remdesivir. Marburg Virus Activity: This candidate also demonstrated potent cross-family activity against Marburg virus (IC50 = 1.04 μΜ). Pan-Filovirus Objective: Decoy is executing generative design campaigns to establish a single, broad-spectrum pan-filovirus D-MAV for pre- and post-exposure prophylaxis against all human-infecting filoviruses. Engineered for Extended Protection & Prophylactic Utility Effective prophylaxis against high-consequence viral pathogens requires sustained drug levels at the site of infection ingress. Beyond optimizing binding potency, Decoy's IMP3ACT platform structurally engineers molecules for extended tissue residence time and long systemic plasma half-lives, with potential for weekly dosing. Addressing the Filovirus Threat and Outbreak Dynamics Filoviruses, including the Ebola and Marburg viruses, cause severe hemorrhagic fevers with historical mortality rates between 40% and 90%. The ongoing outbreak of Bundibugyo virus highlights the critical vulnerability of existing therapeutics, which are largely single-strain specific. Decoy's pan-filovirus approach targets the highly conserved helical fusion core shared across filovirus glycoproteins. By neutralizing the fundamental mechanism of viral entry, Decoy aims to deliver a unified prophylactic solution capable of protecting against Ebola Zaire, Marburg, Sudan, and Bundibugyo viruses simultaneously. "Our recent filovirus data illustrate the speed and precision of our IMP3ACT platform," said Rick Pierce, Chief Executive Officer of Decoy Therapeutics. "In a single optimization cycle, we achieved potent activity against both Ebola Zaire and Marburg viruses. Crucially, by engineering our D-MAVs for extended residence time at key mucosal entry points, we are building therapies designed to offer durable protection. Advancing this program via the FDA Animal Rule path could allow us to efficiently address urgent biodefense needs through non-dilutive funding while expanding our multi-viral pipeline and proprietary computational database." The Animal Rule Regulatory Path The FDA's Animal Rule enables expedited approval for therapeutics targeting lethal pathogens where human efficacy trials are neither ethical nor feasible. Regulatory approval is established through well-controlled animal model efficacy studies combined with human safety and PK evaluation. This streamlined path significantly reduces clinical timelines and overhead, and positions successful candidates for government procurement and Strategic National Stockpile (SNS) inclusion. Decoy intends to fund its D-MAV filovirus and MERS programs primarily through non-dilutive government grants, industry and strategic biodefense partnerships. In addition to addressing an urgent biodefense need, qualifying filovirus approvals offer substantial commercial value through the FDA's Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV) Program: Priority Review Voucher Eligibility: Filoviruses and Lassa fever are designated qualifying tropical diseases under FDA regulations. Upon FDA approval of an eligible filovirus candidate, Decoy would be eligible to receive a PRV. Significant Non-Dilutive Capital Value: A PRV grants priority review status to a subsequent drug application or can be sold to another pharmaceutical company. Recent PRV market transactions have ranged between $100 million and $180 million, offering a major potential source of non-dilutive capital to drive corporate growth. About Decoy Therapeutics, Inc. Decoy Therapeutics (NASDAQ: DCOY) is a biotechnology company developing Designable Multi-Antivirals (D-MAVsTM) powered by its proprietary IMP3ACTTM platform. By combining generative AI structural design with advanced peptide-conjugate chemistry, Decoy creates single therapeutics that target conserved viral entry machinery across entire viral families. Decoy's pipeline includes programs targeting endemic coronaviruses for immunocompromised patients and MERS, paramyxoviruses (RSV, hPIV, Nipah, Measles), and filoviruses (Ebola, Marburg). Key Terms animal rule, half-maximal inhibitory concentration (ic50), priority review voucher, non-dilutive funding, +1 more 5 terms animal rule regulatory "FDA Animal Rule pathway for expedited regulatory approval" A regulatory pathway that allows safety and effectiveness of drugs or vaccines to be judged primarily from well-controlled animal studies when human trials would be unethical or impossible, such as for treatments against rare, lethal exposures. It matters to investors because approval via this route can speed a product to market for urgent or niche needs but carries extra scientific and regulatory risk—think of it as accepting a high-quality dress rehearsal instead of a live show, with requirements for strong animal models and often additional post-approval obligations. half-maximal inhibitory concentration (ic50) medical "low-micromolar half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 1.56" The half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) is the concentration of a drug, antibody, or other molecule required to reduce a specific biological activity (such as enzyme action, cell growth, or receptor signaling) by 50% in a controlled lab assay. It measures potency: lower IC50 means a smaller amount of substance is needed to produce that half‐reduction, like needing less salt to make a soup noticeably less salty. For investors, IC50 helps compare how potent competing drug candidates are and informs early-stage development, dosing expectations, and risk assessments. priority review voucher regulatory "FDA's Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV) Program" A priority review voucher is a transferable regulatory incentive that lets a company move a future drug or device application to the front of the review line, shortening the review period by several months. For investors it matters because the voucher can speed up market access for a high-value product or be sold to other companies for significant cash, acting like a tradable fast-pass that can accelerate revenue or create immediate financial upside. non-dilutive funding financial "actively pursuing non-dilutive government grants" Non-dilutive funding is money a company raises that does not require issuing new shares or reducing existing owners’ percentage ownership, such as grants, certain loans, contract revenue, or licensing deals. It matters to investors because it lets a company finance growth or research without shrinking shareholder stakes or changing control, much like topping up a car’s gas tank instead of selling part of the car to pay for the trip. in vitro technical "demonstrate potent In Vitro Activity Against Ebola Zaire" In vitro describes laboratory tests performed on cells, tissues, or biological molecules outside a living body—literally “in glass,” such as in test tubes or dishes. For investors, in vitro results are an early sign that a drug or technology has a desired effect under controlled conditions, but they don’t guarantee it will work or be safe in animals or people; think of them as a prototype tested on a bench rather than in real-world use. The complete, corrected release follows, with additional details at the end: Decoy Therapeutics Exploring Pan-Filovirus Program via FDA Animal Rule Pathway and Non-Dilutive Funding Next-Generation D-MAVsTM Demonstrate Potent In Vitro Activity Against Ebola Zaire and Marburg Viruses; Targeting High-Value FDA Priority Review Voucher Eligibility CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Decoy Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: DCOY), a biotechnology company pioneering Designable Multi-Antivirals (D-MAVsTM) to target major respiratory and high consequence viral threats, today announced a refined corporate strategy to explore its D-MAVs for additional candidates, including a pan-filovirus program along the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Animal Rule pathway for expedited regulatory approval. Based on recent encouraging discussions, the Company is actively pursuing non-dilutive government grants and public health partnerships to support the preclinical and clinical development of its broad-spectrum biodefense pipeline with monetization potential upon approval via Priority Review Voucher (PRV) opportunities. Platform Velocity & Preclinical Breakthroughs Following the discovery of initial cross-viral activity from Decoy's pan-coronavirus fusion inhibitors against wild-type Ebola Zaire and Lassa fever virus (announced July 27, 2026), Decoy initiated a dedicated program to de novo design filovirus fusion inhibitors using its AI/ML-driven IMP3ACTTM computational engine. Key highlights include: Ebola Zaire Potency: A first-generation de novo candidate achieved a low-micromolar half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 1.56 μΜ against wild-type Ebola Zaire virus in cell-based assays, a > five-fold improvement in potency vs. the pan-coronavirus lead, and a 7-fold improvement over the benchmark antiviral, remdesivir. Marburg Virus Activity: This candidate also demonstrated potent cross-family activity against Marburg virus (IC50 = 1.04 μΜ). Pan-Filovirus Objective: Decoy is executing generative design campaigns to establish a single, broad-spectrum pan-filovirus D-MAV for pre- and post-exposure prophylaxis against all human-infecting filoviruses. Engineered for Extended Protection & Prophylactic Utility Effective prophylaxis against high-consequence viral pathogens requires sustained drug levels at the site of infection ingress. Beyond optimizing binding potency, Decoy's IMP3ACT platform structurally engineers molecules for extended tissue residence time and long systemic plasma half-lives, with potential for weekly dosing. Addressing the Filovirus Threat and Outbreak Dynamics Filoviruses, including the Ebola and Marburg viruses, cause severe hemorrhagic fevers with historical mortality rates between 40% and 90%. The ongoing outbreak of Bundibugyo virus highlights the critical vulnerability of existing therapeutics, which are largely single-strain specific. Decoy's pan-filovirus approach targets the highly conserved helical fusion core shared across filovirus glycoproteins. By neutralizing the fundamental mechanism of viral entry, Decoy aims to deliver a unified prophylactic solution capable of protecting against Ebola Zaire, Marburg, Sudan, and Bundibugyo viruses simultaneously. "Our recent filovirus data illustrate the speed and precision of our IMP3ACT platform," said Rick Pierce, Chief Executive Officer of Decoy Therapeutics. "In a single optimization cycle, we achieved potent activity against both Ebola Zaire and Marburg viruses. Crucially, by engineering our D-MAVs for extended residence time at key mucosal entry points, we are building therapies designed to offer durable protection. Advancing this program via the FDA Animal Rule path could allow us to efficiently address urgent biodefense needs through non-dilutive funding while expanding our multi-viral pipeline and proprietary computational database." The Animal Rule Regulatory Path The FDA's Animal Rule enables expedited approval for therapeutics targeting lethal pathogens where human efficacy trials are neither ethical nor feasible. Regulatory approval is established through well-controlled animal model efficacy studies combined with human safety and PK evaluation. This streamlined path significantly reduces clinical timelines and overhead, and positions successful candidates for government procurement and Strategic National Stockpile (SNS) inclusion. Decoy intends to fund its D-MAV filovirus and MERS programs primarily through non-dilutive government grants, industry and strategic biodefense partnerships. In addition to addressing an urgent biodefense need, qualifying filovirus approvals offer substantial commercial value through the FDA's Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV) Program: Priority Review Voucher Eligibility: Filoviruses and Lassa fever are designated qualifying tropical diseases under FDA regulations. Upon FDA approval of an eligible filovirus candidate, Decoy would be eligible to receive a PRV. Significant Non-Dilutive Capital Value: A PRV grants priority review status to a subsequent drug application or can be sold to another pharmaceutical company. Recent PRV market transactions have ranged between $100 million and $180 million, offering a major potential source of non-dilutive capital to drive corporate growth. About Decoy Therapeutics, Inc. Decoy Therapeutics (NASDAQ: DCOY) is a biotechnology company developing Designable Multi-Antivirals (D-MAVsTM) powered by its proprietary IMP3ACTTM platform. By combining generative AI structural design with advanced peptide-conjugate chemistry, Decoy creates single therapeutics that target conserved viral entry machinery across entire viral families. Decoy's pipeline includes programs targeting endemic coronaviruses for immunocompromised patients and MERS, paramyxoviruses (RSV, hPIV, Nipah, Measles), and filoviruses (Ebola, Marburg). For more information, visit decoytx.com.
